chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from al-Ala' ibn Razin, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about the boundary of the Masjid of the Messenger (peace be upon him and his family), so he (peace be upon him) said: 'From the pillar which is at the head of the grave, to the two pillars from behind the pulpit, on the right of the Qiblah; and it was so that from behind the pulpit there was a path through which the sheep could pass and the man could pass sideways, and the courtyard of the Masjid was from the tiles (al-balaat) to the courtyard (al-sahn).'

key_terms.الْبَلَاطِ: Tiles (specifically stone tiles used in flooring)
key_terms.مَسْجِدُ الرَّسُولِ: The Mosque of the Messenger (Prophet Muhammad SAWW)

ai.seo_question: What are the exact boundaries of the Prophet's Masjid according to Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi provides precise architectural details regarding the original boundaries of the Prophet's Mosque, specifically delineating the sacred space between the pillar near the Prophet's grave and those behind the pulpit. It highlights the practical layout of the early mosque, noting the passageway for livestock and the distinction between the tiled courtyard and the prayer area, reflecting the lived reality of the Prophet's time. This description is crucial for understanding the historical evolution of the Masjid al-Nabawi and the sanctity attributed to its immediate vicinity in Shia jurisprudence.
